entry.e2_PRIMARY: enter at the close of session +1 -- PIT-safe whether the company reported intraday or after the bell
entry.e1_SECONDARY: enter at the close of session 0 -- `event_response_v1`'s convention; a LOOKAHEAD for an after-close reporter, and carried only so the one-session gap is visible

return_bases.raw: the name's own compounded return over the window
return_bases.mkt: raw minus the EW market compounded over the same sessions
return_bases.bo: raw minus BETA x market -- the pre-event market-model beta only, no alpha term. The clean expected-return decomposition.
return_bases.ab: raw minus (alpha + beta x market) -- the FULL fitted pre-event expectation. Over a long clock the alpha term compounds and it carries the name's own pre-announcement run-up, so `ab` is a momentum-charged upper bound on the correction, not the correction. Read `bo` and `ab` together or neither.

sue_definitions.sue: (actual - surpmean) / surpstdev, all three from surpsumu (UNADJUSTED) -- PRIMARY
sue_definitions.sue_ibes: IBES's own suescore column, carried for cross-check
sue_definitions.sue_price: (actual - surpmean) / |CRSP raw prc| on day 0. cfacpr is NOT applied: an unadjusted numerator needs an unadjusted denominator (feedback_a_split_adjusted_numerator_over_a_raw_denominator)

what_it_is: the same machinery with session 0 moved 40 trading sessions AFTER the announcement -- same names, same era, no event. If the reaction signal survives here, it is a two-session price move, not an event family.

BETA_FIRST.note: pre-event market-model betas and alphas of the two extreme deciles. On `raw` and `mkt` neither is removed. On `bo` the BETA is removed and the alpha is not. On `ab` both are, and the alpha row above is the size of what `ab` takes off a 60-session clock -- read it before reading `ab`.
